title: Conditional Probability
author: 696637e49d26457b33c7eff3
chapter_outcomes: Understand and use probability notation. The probability of A = P(A), P(Not A) = P(A′), P(A and B) = P(A ∩ B), P(A or B) = P(A ∪ B)

Calculate probabilities in simple cases. Including selections made with or without replacement. Knowledge of permutations and combinations formulas is not required. Probabilities might be given as fractions, decimals, or percentages.
Find the probability of an event not happening from the probability of it happening. Use of P(A′) = 1 – P(A)
Know and use the addition rule. P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A ∩ B)

Understand the meaning of mutually exclusive events and independent events and apply relevant rules. Use of P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) for mutually exclusive events. Use of P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent events.
Calculate conditional probability in simple cases. Use of P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) is not required.
Use tree diagrams to represent combined events and to aid calculations of probabilities of combined events.
